 JUDGMENT

This judgment arise out of claim petition filed by the claimants against respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "Act") praying for awarding compensation of Rs.51,00,000/- for the death of Sri.Husenappa was died in a road traffic accident that occurred on 11.08.2024.

The case of the claimants in nutshell is that:
On 11.08.2024 at about 04.00pm the deceased was proceeding as a inmate in a Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA-45-0421 with observing all the traffic rules and regulations near Tumkuru- Bangalore NH-48 highway road, near Kuluvanahalli Village, Nelamangala Taluk, Bangalore, a Canter Lorry vehicle bearing Reg.No.MH-13-CU-5297 came with high speed, driven by its drive without observing any traffic rules and regulations, endangering human life and dashed to the petitioner's vehicle.
Due to impact, petitioner sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
Thereafter body was shifted to Nelamangala Govt. hospital and post-mortem was conducted.
After conducting post-mortem was dead body was handed over to the petitioner.
So far they have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards conveyance, hospital, medical, food and nourishment, funeral and obsequies ceremonies.
3. It is the further case of the petitioners that, prior to the date of accident deceased was hale and healthy, he was working as a Mason and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
The deceased was maintaining the family members.

Due to the sudden and untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are terribly and mentally shocked and they have lost bread earner of the family and they have lost love and affection of the deceased.

Hence, the petitioners claims Rs.75,00,000/- as the general damages for death of deceased, for mental shock and agony, for loss of earnings, loss of future earning of the deceased, for loss of love and affections.

The respondent No.1 being the RC owner and the respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the offending Canter Lorry vehicle bearing Reg.No.MH-13-CU-5297 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
4.
The accident in question was taken place due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Canter Lorry bearing Reg.No.MH-13-CU- 5297.
The Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered a case against the driver of the offending Canter Lorry bearing Reg.No.MH-13-CU-5297 in Cr.No.338/2024 p/u/Secs.125(a), 281 & 106 of BNS 2023.
For the aforesaid reasons, the claimants have prayed for awarding total compensation of Rs.51,00,000/- under various heads.

5. In pursuance of the notice, the respondents have appeared through their respective counsels but,
the respondent No.2 alone filed written Statement.

5B. The respondent No.2 has filed the written statement by denying the entire petition averments except admitting the issuance of policy in respect of the respondent No.1 in favour of the Canter Lorry bearing Reg.No.MH-13-CU-5297.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) & 158(6) of MV Act.
It has also denied the involvement of the vehicle in the accident.

Further stated that, the Driver of the Canter Lorry bearing Reg.No.MH-13- CU-5297 did not holding valid and effective DL and also did not possess a valid FC, RC to the vehicle as on the date of accident.
It is contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the
It has also denied the manner of accident.
There is non joinder of necessary parties to the petition.
It is contended that, the accident was occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the tempo where the deceased was traveled.
It has also denied the age, occupation, income of the deceased.

Further contended that the Laxmi vs Santosh Mallayya Bhandari on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169921208/
3 compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.2 prayed to dismiss the petition with costs.
6. Basing on the pleadings of the parties, the following issues are framed for determination.
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, they are the legal representatives and dependants of the deceased Sri.Husenappa S/o Aashappa Pojari @ Aashappa Kurubur ?

2. Whether the petitioners prove that, the deceased Sri.Husenappa S/o Aashappa Pojari @
Aashappa Kurubur, had died due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that occurred on 11-08- 2024 at about 4.00pm, near Tumkuru- Bengaluru NH-48 Highway Road, near Kuluvanahalli village, Nelamangala taluk, due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Canter Lorry bearing Reg.No.MH-13- CU-5297 as alleged?

3. Whether the respondent No.2 proves that, the driver of offending vehicle was not holding effective and valid DL at the time of alleged accident?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as claimed?
If so, what amount and from whom?

5 . What order or Award?

In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner No.1 has examined herself as PW-1 and got marked total 14 documents as Exs.P1 to 14.
The respondents have not led any evidence.
8. I have heard the arguments canvassed by the learned counsel for the parties.

 Issue No.1 : In the affirmative,

11. The PW.1 has reiterated the petition averments in the chief examination.
The PW.1 has been subjected to cross examination.
During the cross examination of PW.1, nothing worthwhile is elicited.
12. To prove the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased, they have produced notarized copy of Aadhar Cards of petitioners and the deceased as per Ex.P.14.
Ex.P.4 Inquest mahazar also shows the names and relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
13. It is undisputed fact that there was a delay in lodging the case.
The First information report indicates that, the informant had not lodged the complaint in time.

In the light of the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India reported in 1 RAVI V/s. BADRINARAYAN AND OTHERS, it is manifestly clear delay in lodging the FIR cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
However, the claim has to be examined with a closer scrutiny, particularly the contents of the FIR.
The First Information report indicates that, the informant had not lodged the complaint as she was busy in providing medical aid to injured.
So, the 1 (2011) 4 SCC 693 informant has shown the reason for lodging the complaint with delay.
Same has been highlighted in the relevant column of FIR.

So,
the reasons assigned by the informant is satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
14. The petitioners have totally relied on the police document to substantiate their claim and also rash and negligent act of the driver of offending vehicle.

The spot mahazar produced by the petitioners are clearly depicts that the driver of the tempo bearing Registration No.KA-45-0421 was drove the same from Thyamalondu side towards Bengaluru-Tumakuru Highway and he used to join the same lane by using path way which was existed at Divider and the driver of the Eicher vehicle has dashed his vehicle to 407 tempo and also the person who was standing at divider.
The police document is clearly depicts that there was negligence on the part of two vehicles viz., Eicher vehicle bearing No.MH.13 CU 5297 and 407 tempo bearing No.KA45-0421.
The Court has framed the issue only on Eicher Vehicle.
But, as I referred there was negligence on the part of two vehicles.
The insurer has also taken a specific plea regarding contributory negligence on the part of tempo.
Apart from the mahazar, the sketch prepared by the investigating officer while drawing spot mahazar indicates that the offending vehicle was dashed to the vehicle bearing Reg No.KA45-0421.
It is the specific case of the insurer that the accident was occurred due to fault of the accused No.2 or driver of the vehicle bearing Reg No.KA45-0421.
It is worth note herein that there was small gap in between the divider where small vehicle can pass it very easily, however the ongoing vehicle and road crossing vehicle have to take minimal care.
The accident spot was Tumakuru - Bangalore NH-48 highway.
As per the police documents itself depicts that the accident spot is being main Road, so it can be presumed that more vehicle moments in the said road.
The accident was occurred at about 4.00pm, normally traffic has so high.
When these being the case, if the driver of the offending Eicher vehicle and the Tempo had taken minimal care, the accident would have been postponed or not occurred.

The police documents and other materials are clearly discloses that the driver of the Tempo driven it without driving license, Insurance, permit having huge number of workers in it and also the Eicher vehicle driver drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed his vehicle to the Tempo and Tempo dashed to the person who was standing on the extreme left side of the road divider.
Further more, the investigating officer had led the charge sheet after thorough investigation against the driver of the Eicher vehicle driver and also RC owner and driver of the Tempo.
16. The contention of the insurance company that the driver of the offending Vehicle was not having valid driving license at the time of accident.

The police have not led charge sheet for offense punishable under section 3 R/w 181 of Motor Vehicles Act and further the insurer had not placed any iota of evidence in this regard.

sentences.text: This Court negatived the said argument by observing that the nature of proof required to establish culpable rashness, punishable under IPC, is more stringent than negligence sufficient under the law of tort to create liability.
The observation made in para 3 of the jud 80 gment would throw some light as to what should be the approach of the Tribunal in motor accident cases.

The same reads thus :
"3. Road accidents are one of the top killers in our country, specially when truck and bus drivers operate nocturnally.
This proverbial recklessness often persuades the courts, as has been observed by us earlier in other cases, to draw an initial presumption in several cases based on the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur.
Accidents Tribunals must take special care to see that innocent victims do not suffer and drivers and owners do not escape liability merely because of some doubt here or some obscurity there.
Save in plain cases, culpability must be inferred from the circumstances where it is fairly reasonable.

The court should not succumb to niceties,
technicalities and mystic maybes.

We are emphasising this aspect because we are often distressed by transport operators getting away with it thanks to judicial laxity,
despite the fact that they do not exercise sufficient disciplinary control over the drivers in the matter of careful driving.
The heavy economic impact of culpable driving of public transport must bring owner and driver to their responsibility to their neighbor.
Indeed, the State must seriously consider no-fault liability by legislation.
A second aspect which pains us is the inadequacy of the compensation or undue parsimony practiced by tribunals.
We must remember that judicial tribunals are State organs and Article 41 of the Constitution lays the jurisprudential foundation for State relief against accidental disablement of citizens.
There is no justification for niggardliness in compensation.
A third factor which is harrowing is the enormous delay in disposal of accident cases resulting in compensation, even if awarded, being postponed by several years.

The States must appoint sufficient number of tribunals Laxmi vs Santosh Mallayya Bhandari on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169921208/
6 and the High Courts should insist upon quick disposals so that the trauma and tragedy already sustained may not be magnified by the injustice of delayed justice.
Many States are unjustly indifferent in this regard."

25. In Dulcina Fernandes [Dulcina Fernandes v. Joaquim Xavier Cruz, (2013) 10 SCC 646 :
(2014) 1 SCC (Civ) 73 : (2014) 1 SCC (Cri) 13] , this Court examined similar situation where the evidence of claimant's eyewitness was discarded by the Tribunal and that the respondent in that case was acquitted in the criminal case concerning the accident. This Court, however, opined that it cannot be overlooked that upon investigation of the case registered against the respondent, prima facie, materials showing negligence were found to put him on trial.

The Court restated the settled principle that the evidence of the claimants ought to be examined by the Tribunal on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and certainly the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied"
18.
The Court cannot adopt strict liability as conducted in a criminal case to prove rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
But there should be prima-facie materials regarding rash and negligence to fix the owner and insurance company for payment of compensation.
Therefore, a straight jacket formula cannot be adopted in accepting the rash and negligence on the part of driver of the insured.

15. Secondly, even if the some persons were persons were come to rescue the injured they may refrain to intimate the police based on their past experience with the investigation agency or general impression they carry about the police.
16. Under such circumstances, expecting an eye witnesses to be present in each and every case, is far from reality."
Though, the petitioners have not examined the eye witnesses is not fatal to their case.
The materials on record clearly indicates that the accident has occurred due to negligence of drivers of tempo and Eicher.
Hence, it is appears to Court that the driver of the tempo bearing registration No.KA45-0421 and Eicher bearing Registration No.MH13-CU-5297 have contributed to the accident at the ratio of 40:60.

Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative, issue No.2 partly in affirmative and Issue No.3 in the negative.

sentences.text: In the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi and others, if an injured person below 40 years, then 40% of future prospects should be added to his monthly income.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So, the monthly income of deceased is Rs.16,500/- and the deceased comes below the age of 40 years slab then 40% of future prospects of his income would come to Rs.6,600/- then after adding the future prospects to his total income it comes to Rs.23,100/-.
As per Sarala Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 16.
Hence, the petitioners are dependents of the deceased.
If there are exceeding 6 dependents, then 1/5th of the income has to deducted towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased.
Then the total income of the deceased would come Rs.18,480/- (Rs.23,100/- - Rs.4,620/- = Rs.18,480/-).
The loss of dependency is calculated as below.
Rs.18,480/- (monthly income) x 12 x 16 (multiplier) =Rs.35,48,160=00.
This is just and proper compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
LOSS OF ESTATE 21.
As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Pranay Sethi case in case of death in the maximum the Court can award Rs.18,150/- in lump sum under the head of loss of estate.
FUNERAL EXPENSES 22.
In view of the Pranay Sethi's case this tribunal has no option but to award Rs.18,150/- under this head.
Except these heads the claimants are not entitled for any compensation.
LOSS OF CONSORTIUM 23.

In view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India reported in 4(2018) 18 SCC 130,
the Petitioner No.1 is being wife, petitioner Nos.2 to 5 being children and Petitioner Nos.6 & 7 are the parents of the deceased are entitled for '"Spousal Consortium' & 'Parental Consortium' and 'Filial Consortium' respectively.
Hence a sum of Rs.3,38,800/- (Rs.48,400/- each) is awarded under this head.

sentences.text: It is not the case of the insurer that the offending vehicle viz Eicher was not having insurance at the time of accident.
As I referred above, the materials on record clearly indicates that the accident has occurred due to negligence of drivers of tempo and Eicher.
And the tribunal has fixed the negligence on the driver of the tempo bearing Reg. No.KA45-0421 and Eicher bearing Registration No.MH13CU 5297 at the ratio of 40:60.

Hence, the respondent No.2 or insurer of Eicher vehicle bearing No.MH13 CU 5297 is liable to pay 60% of the total compensation in precisely an amount of Rs.23,53,956=00 (Rs.39,23,260  60  100) with interest.

Like wise the owner of the tempo bearing Reg.No.KA-45-0421 viz., Basavaraj S/o Chandraiah, No.42, 1st Cross, Pattegarapalya, Sharavathi Nagar, Bengaluru is liable to pay the 40%
of the total compensation amount in precisely an amount of Rs.15,69,304=00 (Rs.39,23,260  40  100) with interest to petitioners.
The petitioners have not arrayed the owner of the tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-45-0421 as Respondent in this case.
However, the petitioner are at liberty to recover the said portion of the amount from the owner of the Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-45-0421 with due process of law.

26. APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION:
The claimants Nos.1 to 7 are being the wife, minor children and parents of the deceased.
Hence, they are entitled at the ratio of 40:10:10:10:10:10:10 respectively in the total compensation with accrued interest.
On deposit of compensation, the claimant No.1 is entitled to withdraw 70% of her share and remaining amount shall be deposited in her name for a period of 3 years in any Nationalized Bank.
On deposit of the share of the Claimant Nos.2 to 5 shall be kept as FD in their names till they attains the age of majority with a liberty to withdraw interest.
On deposit of the share of the Claimant Nos.6 & 7, entire amount shall be released in their names on proper identification through e-payment.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.4 partly in Affirmative.
27. Issue No.5:-
In view of my findings to the above issues, the claimants are entitled for the compensation at the at rate of 6% P.A. from the respondent No.2.
